jobs.title: Recreation - Aquatics Supervisor - Programming
jobs.description:
This posting will remain continuously until filled.

The Town of Castle Rock’s future and the quality of that depend on the choices we make today. Do you want to be part of a team that make decisions that work now while preserving and protecting Castle Rock’s identity and quality of life for the future? We value teamwork
, cooperation
, and quality communication
. We strive to provide exceptional public service to our customers and encourage creativity and innovation. We welcome all that share those values to apply.

Working For The Town Of Castle Rock Includes

The opportunity to make a difference in our community
Career Advancement Programs
Employee well-being program
Competitive total compensation with an excellent benefits package
Free membership to the MAC or Recreation Center
Public Service Student Loan Forgiveness eligible employer

Position Overview

The Town of Castle Rock has an outstanding opportunity for an Aquatics Supervisor - Programming
in our Parks and Recreations department. This position organizes, coordinates, implements, and evaluates comprehensive aquatic programming for the Town's aquatics division. Employees in this classification perform administrative, supervisory, and program management work. The position is responsible for managing a comprehensive swim lesson program for participants of all ages and abilities; coordinating a competitive developmental swim team; and supporting other competitive, instructional, and recreational aquatic teams, programs, and activities.

This position is responsible for recruiting, hiring, training, scheduling, supervising, evaluating, and retaining part-time aquatics programming staff, including swim lesson instructors, coaches, and part-time program coordinators. The position serves as a member of the aquatics administrative staff and may be required to serve as a designated on-call staff member. The position also assists with the daily operations of aquatics facilities as needed. Work is performed under the general supervision of the Aquatics Senior Supervisor. Performs duties in a manner consistent with the stated values of the organization.

Essential Duties And Responsibilities

Performs lead-level duties that include instructing, assigning, reviewing, and planning the work of others; monitoring standards; coordinating activities; allocating personnel; and providing feedback.
Plans, organizes, implements, supervises, and evaluates a comprehensive swim lesson program serving participants of all ages, abilities, and skill levels.
Develops and maintains swim lesson curriculum, class levels, instructor expectations, participant evaluation standards, and program progression guidelines.
Coordinates swim lesson registration, class schedules, instructor assignments, participant placement, waitlists, transfers, and program communications.
Manages a competitive developmental swim team, including season planning, coach assignments, participant registration, practice schedules, meets, team communications, and program evaluation.
Supports, develops, and coordinates other competitive, instructional, and recreational aquatic teams, programs, clinics, camps, and activities.
Recruits, hires, trains, schedules, supervises, evaluates, and supports part-time aquatics programming staff, including swim lesson instructors, coaches, and part-time program coordinators.
Develops and implements staff training programs related to swim instruction, coaching standards, customer service, safety, emergency response, program administration, and Town policies and procedures.
Promotes staff retention through ongoing communication, coaching, recognition, professional development, and effective supervision.
Enters, maintains, and updates aquatic programming information in the Town's registration software, including course descriptions, schedules, fees, capacities, prerequisites, staff assignments, and program notes.
Monitors program enrollment, participation trends, staffing levels, revenue, expenses, and customer feedback to recommend program improvements.
Communicates with participants, parents, staff, coaches, instructors, and community members; responds to inquiries and resolves concerns regarding aquatic programs, instructors, coaches, teams, registrations, and facilities.
Assists in the management of aquatic facilities and daily operations as needed; resolves staff, participant, and facility-related concerns.
Assists with vendor contract management.
Serves as a member of the aquatics administrative staff and participates in staff meetings, planning efforts, policy implementation, and operational decision-making.
May serve as a designated on-call staff member and respond to operational, staffing, safety, or facility needs outside of regular work hours.
Supervises children and other program participants enrolled in aquatic activities; provides appropriate guidance and ensures a safe, positive, and inclusive program environment.
Assists in preparing, monitoring, and administering aquatic program budgets, including revenue projections, expenditures, staffing costs, supplies, and equipment needs.
Prepares biweekly time sheets, purchase orders, purchase requests, vouchers, reports, and other administrative documents.
Purchases program supplies and equipment; communicates with vendors and assists with procurement processes.
Assists with marketing and promotion of aquatic programs, swim lessons, teams, and special events.
Performs disaster drills; administers First Aid and performs CPR when needed.
Ensures compliance with applicable safety standards, Town policies, aquatic facility rules, and program procedures.
Performs clerical and administrative functions related to aquatics programming and facility operations.
Assists with aquatic facility rentals, special events, swim meets, and community programs as needed.
Assists with cleaning, organizing, and maintaining recreation and aquatic program areas.
Provides support for front desk, lifeguard, pool operations, and facility staff as needed.
Performs other duties as assigned.

Minimum Qualifications

An equivalent combination of education, training, and experience that demonstrates required knowledge, skills, and abilities may be considered.

Education:
Bachelor's Degree in recreation management, community recreation, aquatic resources, sports recreation or in a related field.

Experience:
At least two (2) years of professional experience that provides broad knowledge of aquatic programming, swim lesson administration, competitive or developmental swim team operations, public recreation, community resources, and the administrative aspects of the work or in a closely related field, including one (1) year of staff supervision in the aquatic field; or an equivalent combination of education, training, and experience. Experience using recreation registration software or a similar program management software is preferred.

Licenses And/or Certifications Required

a valid Colorado Driver's License
CPR and First Aid Training Certificate or the ability to obtain within 30 days of hire
Lifeguard Certification or the ability to obtain within 30 days of hire
Swim Lesson Instructor, Water Safety Instructor, Coaching, and/or Aquatics programming certifications are preferred or have the ability to obtain within 90 days of hire.

Knowledge, Skills, And Abilities

Knowledge of principles of effective administration, including planning, coordinating, evaluating, supervising, and leading staff.
Knowledge of aquatic programming principles, including swim lesson instruction, skill progression, participant assessment, class placement, and inclusive programming for all ages and abilities.
Knowledge of competitive and developmental swim team operations, including coaching practices, meet coordination, team communication, and participant development.
Knowledge of the characteristics and needs of children, youth, adults, seniors, individuals with disabilities, and other aquatic program participants.
Knowledge of principles and techniques of short- and long-range recreational and aquatic program planning.
Knowledge of staff recruitment, hiring, onboarding, training, scheduling, supervision, evaluation, and retention practices.
Knowledge of customer service practices and methods for responding to citizen concerns with tact, professionalism, and courtesy.
Knowledge of basic budget administration, program revenue tracking, expense monitoring, and purchasing procedures.
Knowledge of aquatic safety practices, emergency response procedures, risk management principles, and applicable facility rules.
Skill in written and oral communication for effective expression, clarity, instruction, and public interaction.
Skill in teaching, coaching, training, mentoring, and evaluating aquatic staff.
Skill in planning, organizing, and implementing aquatic programs, swim lessons, teams, clinics, events, and activities.
Skill in using recreation registration software to create programs, manage registrations, update rosters, track enrollment, and communicate with participants.
Skill in operating standard office equipment, computers, software systems, and aquatic program equipment.
Skill in performing and instructing CPR and First Aid.
Ability to exercise sound judgment and make independent decisions in accordance with established Town policies and procedures.
Ability to respond to citizen complaints and concerns with considerable tact, courtesy, and professionalism.
Ability to establish and maintain effective working relationships with supervisors, support staff, part-time employees, contracted personnel, volunteers, participants, parents, vendors, and other departments.
Ability to plan, prioritize, and manage multiple programs, staff schedules, deadlines, and operational needs.
Ability to evaluate program effectiveness and recommend improvements based on participation trends, community needs, safety considerations, budget impacts, and customer feedback.
Ability to perform addition, subtraction, multiplication, and division; calculate decimals and percentages; utilize principles of fractions; and interpret graphs, reports, and program data.
Ability to perform coordinated movements involving operating a computer terminal, pool equipment, recreation equipment, aquatic program equipment, and related tools.

Physical Demands

Sedentary work for long periods of time
Occasional physical work lifting no more than 10 pounds
Occasional lifting, carrying, walking and standing
Occasionally required to use hands to finger, handle or feel objects, tools or controls; reach with hands and arms; and stop, kneel, crouch or crawl
Frequent hand/eye coordination to operate personal computer and office equipment
Vision for reading, recording and interpreting information
Speech communication and hearing to maintain communication with employees and citizens
Ability to work flexible hours, including nights and/or weekends as needed.
Ability to drive to and physically access various parks and recreation facilities

Work Environment

Works primarily in a clean, comfortable environment
Events may take place in a variety of settings, including outdoors in all weather conditions.
Periods of time in the pool and pool area with exposure to temperature extremes, varying weather conditions, chemicals, water and other conditions found in the pool area

Equipment Used

Uses standard office equipment including a personal computer system
This position may require the incumbent to occasionally use personal equipment (e.g. vehicle, cell phone, tools, etc.) in the course of their employment.

Must satisfactorily complete a criminal background check prior to commencing employment.

The Town of Castle Rock is an Equal Opportunity Employer.

jobs.title: Supervisor, Project Engineering
jobs.description:
About Carrier

Carrier Global Corporation, global leader in intelligent climate and energy solutions, is committed to creating innovations that bring comfort, safety and sustainability to life. Through cutting-edge advancements in climate solutions such as temperature control, air quality and transportation, we improve lives, empower critical industries and ensure the safe transport of food, life-saving medicines and more. Since inventing modern air conditioning in 1902, we lead with purpose: enhancing the lives we live and the world we share. We continue to lead because of our world-class, inclusive workforce that puts the customer at the center of everything we do. For more information, visit corporate.carrier.com or follow Carrier on social media at @Carrier.

About The Role

Leads and coordinates the engineering team supporting new product introductions, engineering changes, and product improvement initiatives. Ensures projects meet safety, quality, cost, delivery, and compliance objectives while providing technical leadership and project oversight. Develops team capabilities and supports organizational readiness for future business needs.

Key Responsibilities

As a Supervisor, Project Engineering, you'll be responsible for:

New Product Introduction (NPI)

Coordinate execution of NPI activities across assigned programs or product families.
Monitor project deliverables, action items, risks, and timing to support successful launch execution.
Support pilot builds, launch readiness reviews, validation activities, and production ramp-up.
Identify, communicate, and mitigate risks associated with product and process launches.

Engineering Change Management

Oversee execution and follow-up of Engineering Change Notices (ECNs) across assigned products or programs.
Ensure impacts to BOM, manufacturing process, tooling, inventory, validation, cost, and schedule are evaluated and communicated.
Coordinate change implementation with Engineering, Manufacturing, Supply Chain, Planning, Quality, and Operations.
Monitor ECN timing, approval status, documentation, implementation, and closure activities.
Prioritize engineering changes based on business impact, launch timing, and operational risk.

Requirements

We are looking for people who are proactive. If this is you, get in touch.

Education

As a minimum you must have:

Bachelor's degree in mechanical engineering, Manufacturing Engineering, Industrial Engineering, Mechatronics Engineering, or a related technical discipline.

Experience

4-5 years of experience in Product Engineering, New Product Introduction (NPI), Sustaining Engineering, Manufacturing Engineering, Product Development, or Technical Project Leadership.
1-3 years of experience leading projects, coordinating technical teams, or providing functional supervision is required or strongly preferred.

Technical Knowledge

Product development lifecycle and New Product Introduction processes.
ERP systems, preferably SAP, and CAD systems such as Creo, SolidWorks, or equivalent.
Engineering Change Management, BOM structure, technical documentation, and implementation planning.
Root Cause Analysis, corrective actions, structured problem solving, APQP, DFMEA, PFMEA, and control plans.

Language

Advanced English proficiency, both written and verbal.

Although not necessary, it would be nice if you have:

Experience supervising or coordinating engineers or technical resources.
Experience supporting NPI launches within HVAC, refrigeration, appliance, or manufacturing industries.
Experience working with global engineering teams and manufacturing sites.

Benefits

We offer a competitive total rewards package that may include other benefits and well‑being programs. Offerings vary by role and location and are designed to support employees’ health, security, and success.

If you require a reasonable accommodation to complete the application process, participate in an interview, or otherwise engage in the hiring process, please contact us at Carrier.Recruiting@carrier.com. We will make every effort to meet your needs in accordance with applicable laws.

Carrier is An Equal Opportunity/Affirmative Action Employer. All qualified applicants will receive consideration for employment without regard to race, color, religion, sex, sexual orientation, gender identity, national origin, disability or veteran status, age or any other federally protected class.

Rejoignez nos plus de 33 000 collaborateurs répartis dans près de 100 pays et partagez la joie de transformer le destin d'enfants vulnérables !

C'est Là Que Vous Intervenez

En tant que coordinateur(trice) du programme Cash Academy,
vous contribuerez à la mise en œuvre efficace et à l'amélioration continue du programme DMT Cash Academy en coordonnant les activités de formation relatives aux programmes de bons d'achat et de paiement (CVP), les initiatives d'apprentissage numérique et les systèmes de soutien aux apprenants. Vous gérerez les calendriers de formation, les processus de candidature et d'inscription, le suivi des apprenants et la coordination avec les formateurs, les mentors et les étudiants à travers le monde.

Vous participerez également au développement et à l'amélioration des modules de cours numériques, des outils d'animation et des ressources pédagogiques, tout en veillant à la rigueur des processus de documentation, de reporting, d'assurance qualité et de gestion des connaissances. Vous contribuerez au renforcement des capacités mondiales de World Vision en matière de formation continue et à la promotion de solutions d'apprentissage innovantes, de haute qualité et adaptables à grande échelle.

Les Exigences Comprennent

Licence en développement international, éducation, sciences sociales, études humanitaires ou discipline connexe.
Au moins 5 ans d'expérience pertinente dans le domaine humanitaire/du développement, dont au minimum 2 ans dans le domaine des violences conjugales et de l'aide alimentaire.
Une certification professionnelle en matière d'aide financière par espèces et bons d'achat, telle que CaLP, est souhaitable.
Solide connaissance du CVP, de la programmation axée sur le marché et des normes et principes humanitaires applicables.
Expérience avérée dans le développement et la diffusion de contenus et de modules de cours numériques utilisant les plateformes et technologies d'apprentissage en ligne pertinentes.
La maîtrise de l'anglais est requise ; le français et/ou l'arabe sont un atout.

Postuler ici.

Ce poste vous convient-il ?

avant la date limite du 16 juin 2026.

jobs.title: Training Coordinator
jobs.description:
Company Description
DYNE Hospitality Group, founded in December 2017, is the largest Tropical Smoothie Café franchisee, with locations across Arkansas, Alabama, Georgia, Florida, Oklahoma, Missouri, Kansas, and Texas. The company’s mission is to create opportunities by empowering team members to use their unique talents and strengths. DYNE focuses on sustained growth as the primary measure of success and emphasizes operational excellence in every café. Team members are valued like family, provided with resources to grow, and encouraged to deliver exceptional guest experiences. Applicants can learn more about DYNE Hospitality Group and available opportunities by visiting the company website.
Role Description
The Training Coordinator role is a full-time hybrid position based in the Greater Fayetteville, AR area, with some work-from-home flexibility. This role is responsible for coordinating training programs for café teams, including scheduling sessions, organizing materials, and ensuring timely communication with managers and trainees. The Training Coordinator will support the design and delivery of employee training initiatives, track participation and performance, and maintain training records and documentation. Day-to-day tasks include collaborating with operations leaders to identify training needs, assisting with onboarding for new team members, and helping to improve training content and processes. The role also involves monitoring training effectiveness, preparing reports, and contributing to a consistent, high-quality guest experience across all locations.
Qualifications

Strong skills in Training Coordination and Training, including scheduling, organizing sessions, and managing training logistics.
Experience in Training & Development and Employee Training, with the ability to support onboarding and ongoing learning programs.
Effective Communication skills, including clear written and verbal communication with team members at all levels.
Ability to build relationships with café leaders and team members, fostering a supportive training environment.
Attention to detail and strong organizational skills for maintaining training records and tracking progress.
Proficiency with basic office software and learning tools (e.g., spreadsheets, presentation software, learning platforms).
Prior experience in hospitality, restaurants, or retail operations is beneficial.
High school diploma or equivalent required; additional education or certifications in training, HR, or organizational development are a plus.
Ability to work in a hybrid environment in the Greater Fayetteville, AR area and travel to local cafes as needed.
